Analysing Phone Usage on the Bus

What is my data about?

This data explores the mobile phone usage among people on the bus. It was collected by observing the proportion of people using their phones at different times of days, across weekends and weekdays. Analyzing these patterns allowed us to see how phone usage changes depending on the time of day or type of day, giving insight to our behaviors.

The things I have analysed are:

  1. Average proportion of people using phones by Time of Day
  2. Average proportion of people using phones by Hour of Day
  3. Average proportion of people using phones on Weekends vs Weekdays

Phone usage by Time of Day

The bar chart shows the average proportion of people using their phones at different times of the day. Early morning (5am to 9am) had the highest average, suggesting people are more likely to use their phones during the morning to maybe check messages, emails, scroll social media or to just pass time.

Afternoon travel (12pm to 5pm) showed relatively high phone usage, but as the day goes on it slightly decreases.This could be due to people being more tired and just wanting to rest on the bus.

Morning (9am - 12pm) had the lowest average phone usage, suggesting shorter travel times.

This chart suggests that phone usage on the bus changes depending on the time of day.

Bar chart of average proportion of phone usage by time of day

Phone usage by hour of day.

The line chart shows the average proportion of people on their phones on the bus at different hours of the day. Phone usage is higher around 8am suggesting people are more likely to use their phones to check messages, emails and other stuff during the morning.

Around 10am a few hours past, phone usage decreasing suggesting less reliance on phones during those times.

After 6pm, we see another increase in phone usage, reaching a peak at 8pm. This suggests that people in the evening are likely to use their phones for entertainment on the way home from work, school or anywhere else.

This chart shows that phone usage on public transport changes depending on the hour of the day.

Line chart of average proportion of phone usage by Hour of Day

Phone usage on Weekends vs Weekdays

This boxplot shows the distribution of phone usage on the bus on weekdays compared to weekends. Weekday phone usage appears to have a higher median proportion than weekends, this suggests that people are more likely to use their phones during the weekday. This could be because weekdays are associated with school and work, meaning people would check their phones for messages, emails, notifications and such.

We can see that phone usage on the weekends have a lower median overall, but there is variation suggesting that phone usage remains common but it just less consistent depending on the purpose of their travel. The weekday data has a wider spread suggesting phone usage varies more on weekdays, because of different times and schedules.

Overall, this boxplot suggests phone usage on the bus is influenced by the type of day, weekend or weekday. This reflects people’s routine and travel behavior.
